mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is causally associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reduces the cost of capital for corporations and increases the relative attractiveness of equities versus fixed income.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward returns is >= 0 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 7.5% over the past 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which is causally linked to higher corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is below 7.5%, the average 5-day forward return is not positive (mean <= 0) in more than 40% of observations over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages indicates robust consumer demand, which is causally linked to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages, the average 60-day forward return is not positive (mean <= 0) in more than 40% of observations over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During the early expansion phase of the business cycle (characterized by rising industrial production), a positive change in industrial production (INDPRO) is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it signals strengthening economic activity and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: In the early expansion phase (defined by INDPRO growth > 0.5% and UNRATE < 7.0%), the average 20-day forward return is not positive (mean <= 0) in more than 40% of observations over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL > 235) signals persistent inflationary pressures, which are associated with an increased likelihood of Federal Reserve rate hikes and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL is above 235, the average 5-day forward return is not negative (mean >= 0) in more than 40% of observations over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) is causally associated with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as it reflects sustained consumer spending strength.
failure_condition: Rank IC between RSAFS and 60-day forward returns is >= 0 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST > 900) signals robust economic activity and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as it indicates strong residential construction and related sector growth.
failure_condition: When HOUST is above 900, the average 5-day forward return is not positive (mean <= 0) in more than 40% of observations over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During the labor market recovery phase (characterized by declining unemployment and rising nonfarm payrolls), a positive change in employment (PAYEMS) is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as it signals improving consumer spending and corporate profitability.
failure_condition: In the labor market recovery phase (defined by UNRATE decline > 0.2% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% over 3 months), the average 60-day forward return is not positive (mean <= 0) in more than 40% of observations over a 3-year rolling window.
